correctness.rationale: The exact Gram block computation for \(F^*F\) proves removal of \(V_2\) and unitary decomposition off \(\ker V_1^*\). The polar splitting of \(T\) gives the explicit commuting \(B(S)\); the continuous orthogonal diagonalizer \(W(s)\) was checked algebraically and extends to \(s=0\). The resulting direct-sum identity exactly yields zero/unit eigenmultiplicities. The Schur-complement identity for \(\lambda\ne1\) and factored matrix at \(\lambda=1\) prove the essential spectrum without missing the exceptional point. Operator-ideal equivalence follows from continuous positive ratios \((\varphi(s)-1)/s\) and \((1-\varphi(s)^{-1})/s\) bounded above and below for bounded s. The embedded finite complex-matrix checker passed 6858 numerical comparisons; it does not prove the infinite theorem.

Garcia (2009) and Raghupathi (2012) cover nonexceptional scalar spectral mapping and parts of the unit-point invertibility problem; Nag–Golla (2026) covers norms, attainment and Fredholmness. value.rationale: An exact unitary classification of the entire singular spectral measure, including continuous spectrum and both exceptional eigenspace multiplicities, is a natural invariant not furnished by norm/minimum formulas. It sharply distinguishes V2-dependent Fredholm index from V2-independent modulus, settles the central unit-point essential phenomenon in non-Fredholm cases, and determines all Schatten perturbation costs with a complete if-and-only-if. The result is structural and holds for arbitrary bounded corners and arbitrary isometric diagonal pairs, rather than one selected example or a small numerical gain.
